native_review_note: Spanish strings are a careful draft; a native speaker reviews them before any real pilot (the same rule as card.es.json).

format.summary: Card-side text for the 'money you may be missing' part of the student card (the fixed part `unlocked`, under the hero). The programs engine (data/rules/programs_2026.json) decides every status and every number; these templates only speak. Code fills each {placeholder} with a display value and never writes wording of its own. Nothing here is spoken on the phone: the call and its sentence keys do not change.
format.strings: strings.<key> = one template. Keys are dotted names: ui.* (widget labels), share.text, q.<question> and q.<question>.<choice> (the card questions; choice ids as in the rules table), program.<id> (names), <program>.* (program lines and notes; the rules table names these keys in status_rules notes, note_rules, notes_always and calfresh_link.text_key), list_only.<id> (one line each in list_only mode, never with an amount), apply.* (button labels; urls in links), pf.* (prefill rows: screen names stay in English, as on the official forms) and care.utility_conflict (the gray console note). en and es have the same keys and the same {placeholders} in each key.
format.programs: programs.<id> is the same in both languages. name: the name key. lines: status -> line key, or status -> {variant: key}. notes: every note key the program can show. UnlockedProgram.notes = the line's engine note_keys (golden order), then, in full mode for plan lines (likely, maybe, check, coverage), the table's calfresh_link.text_key, then calfresh.basis on the calfresh line and tax.basis on the tax_credits line; a key equal to the line is not repeated; list_only shows no notes. Engine note_keys (golden) stay as they are. list_only: the key used in list_only mode. value_text: status -> the short value text shown next to the name (null = none). chip: status -> chip key. apply: the button label key; the url is links[apply], opened in a new tab, except CalFresh: its label is apply.calfresh_steps and its link '#today_action' is the in-page link to the card's today_action block (same tab, no external icon; docs/UI_SPEC.md A4.2 row 2b). sources: display order; the first one is shown with ui.source.
format.variants: care likely/maybe: 'alone' when bill_split is 1 (one person pays the bill), else 'shared' (the line names the split). tax_credits likely: variant no_child -> 'both' when the CalEITC anchor value and the federal no-child EITC are both above 0, 'state_only' when only CalEITC is, 'federal_only' when only the federal credit is; variant parent -> 'parent' when the Young Child Tax Credit is above 0, else 'parent_federal_only'. tax_credits maybe: 'any', or 'small' when the computed value is 0 (the table's downgrade). A note key that is also the line (status note) is not repeated under notes.
format.budgets: Words per string, counted as in contracts/check_examples.py (a whitespace token with a letter or digit; a {placeholder} is one word): question 18, choice 5, line 30, note 25, share 30, footnote 25 (docs: the upgrade's card-side budgets), plus label 18 (ui.*), button 5 (apply.*), name 6 (program.*), prefill 18 (pf.*), console 30. check_content.py checks every string.
format.money: Money placeholders get '$' and a thousands comma. found, calfresh_year, claimed, value, lo, hi, fed and household are display values floored to $10; share is floored to $100; calfresh_month, bill and amount are exact dollars (the monthly estimate, the assumed bill, a slot value). The sum of the counted display values is found, so the parts on screen add up to the headline.
format.honesty: Every amount is worded 'about', 'up to' or 'maybe' (es: unos, hasta, quizá). A line that rests on an assumed input shows the assumption (CARE: the assumed bill and split). A ceiling says 'up to' (LifeLine: $19 a month is the most; a cheaper plan saves less). Medi-Cal is coverage, never cash, never '$0 premium' and never a dental or vision promise ('at no cost for most students today'). Tax credits are credits from the 2025 state tables, not refund amounts (tax.basis). The output guard (guards.json) blocks 'you will get', 'you'll save $', 'you're covered/enrolled', 'free money' and the rest; every string here passes it, filled and unfilled.
format.prefill: pf rows: question_key + answer_key, or question_key + answer_from. answer_from 'answer:<question>' -> pf.answer.<question>.<choice>; 'fact:earned_monthly' -> pf.answer.earned_monthly; 'fact:household_food' -> pf.answer.household_food.<value>; 'fact:people_in_home' -> pf.answer.people_in_home; 'fact:half_time' -> pf.answer.half_time.<true|false>. A row whose answer is unknown (question unanswered, slot empty) is left out. Nothing asks for an SSN or immigration status.
format.chips: Under the bar: ui.coverage_chip (Medi-Cal coverage), ui.maybe_chip (each maybe line with a value), ui.check_chip.<program> (a check line with a range). The bar text is ui.total + ' · ' + ui.claimed.
format.share: share.text only in full mode with found > 0. {share} is floored to $100 and {site} is the public site origin. It never carries the card url, the token, the case code or any answer.
format.verify: Screen and button names on the official sites were not all re-read on 2026-10-01: the BenefitsCal programs and tax screens, the Clipper START photo-ID list, the LifeLine household worksheet and the SF State VITA intake. They are worded loosely on purpose; the rules table lists them as unverified.

calfresh_year.fill: 12 x the monthly CalFresh estimate, floored to $10

n.fill: ui.question_count: number of questions; care.*: people splitting the bill (bill_split)

value.fill: the line's display value (yearly, floored to $10)

lo.fill: the low end of a check range (floored to $10)

hi.fill: the high end of a check range (floored to $10)

fed.fill: federal Lifeline, money.horizon_months x the row's monthly, floored to $10

household.fill: the CARE saving for the whole home (floored to $10)

bill.fill: the assumed monthly PG&E bill (care.rates default)

date.fill: ui.apply_by: server-formatted month and day, no weekday; ui.source: the source's date_text

site.fill: the public site origin (never the card url)
